'''Curie's principle''', or '''Curie's symmetry principle''', is a maxim about cause and effect formulated by [[Pierre Curie]] in 1894:<ref>{{cite journal | last=Curie | first=P. |author-link=Pierre Curie| title=Sur la symétrie dans les phénomènes physiques, symétrie d'un champ électrique et d'un champ magnétique | journal=Journal de Physique Théorique et Appliquée | publisher=EDP Sciences | volume=3 | issue=1 | year=1894 | issn=0368-3893 | doi=10.1051/jphystap:018940030039300 | pages=393–415|url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/jpa-00239814/document|language=fr|trans-title=On the symmetries of physical phenomenae, the electric field, and the magnetic field}}</ref>
{{quote|the symmetries of the causes are to be found in the
effects.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Castellani |first1=Elena |last2=Jenann |first2=Ismael |date=December 2016 |title=Which Curie's Principle? |url=https://repository.arizona.edu/bitstream/10150/625244/1/687933.pdf |journal=Philosophy of Science |volume=83 |issue=5 |pages= 1002–1013|doi=10.1086/687933 |hdl=10150/625244 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ismael |first1=Jenann |date=February 1997 |title=Curie's Principle |journal=[[Synthese]] |volume=110 |issue=2 |pages= 167–190|doi=10.1023/A:1004929109216 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chalmers |first1=A.F. |date=May 1970 |title=Curie's Principle |journal=[[British Journal for the Philosophy of Science]] |volume=21 |issue=2 |pages= 133–148|doi=10.1093/bjps/21.2.133 }}</ref>}}

The idea was based on the ideas of [[Franz Ernst Neumann]] and [[Bernhard Minnigerode]]. Thus, it is sometimes known as the '''Neumann–Minnigerode–Curie principle'''.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Brandmüller | first=J. | title=An extension of the Neumann–Minnigerode–Curie principle | journal=Computers & Mathematics with Applications | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=12 | issue=1–2 | year=1986 | issn=0898-1221 | doi=10.1016/0898-1221(86)90143-4 | pages=97–100|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82370259.pdf| doi-access=free }}</ref>

Later physicists have interpreted Curie's principle in the context of thermodynamics. Dynamics close to equilibrium are described by a set of transport coefficients whose symmetries must match the symmetries of the system, according to Curie's principle. <ref>{{cite book | last1=de Groot| first1= S. R.| last2= Mazur| first2 = P.| title = Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics | publisher = Dover Publications| year=2013| ISBN= 9780486153506| pages =31}}</ref>
